purpose: Virginia insurance settlements linking pricing, notice, network, and claims failures to reported restitution and prospective correction while preserving individual recovery and trust as open.

events.method: Structured extraction from the Virginia SCC public settlement summary
events.missingness: No policyholder identifiers, individual payment, premium correction, coverage continuity, residual loss, trust, or switching
events.exposure: Esurance reportedly increased premiums or charged points after accidents without required notice
events.alternatives_before_action: Policyholders could contact the insurer, seek regulatory review, change coverage, or remain; individual choices are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Reported premium/rating harm and approximately $2 million aggregate restitution; person-level restoration is not verified
events.choice_or_response: The insurer self-reported the issue, offered settlement, and accepted a corrective plan; policyholder response is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Esurance controlled rating/notice operations; SCC controlled investigation and settlement acceptance
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Restitution plus additional impact analysis before new rate factors and continued notice monitoring
events.remedy_receipt: The SCC reports aggregate restitution paid; individual receipt and adequacy are not verified
events.durability_followup: Future premium accuracy, notice compliance, coverage continuity, trust, switching, and residual loss remain open
events.immediate_outcome: Aggregate restitution and prospective process correction are reported
events.protected_outcome: Some policyholders may have received compensation and future errors may be reduced; household protection is not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Individual underpayment, delayed receipt, remaining premium burden, and coverage disruption cannot be identified
events.cost_risk_transfer: Settlement shifts some correction cost to the insurer while recipient timing and residual-loss risk remain unobserved
events.later_outcome: No individual receipt, corrected premium, renewed coverage, recurrence, trust, switching, or exit is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: Regulatory fault attribution is visible; policyholder fairness and trust judgments are not
events.public_or_collective_response: State oversight is visible; policyholder organizing and political action are not
events.counterexample: Aggregate payment and a corrective plan can coexist with unknown individual receipt and unresolved coverage effects
events.source_and_uncertainty: Virginia SCC public settlement summary; aggregate payment and corrective-plan statements are regulator-reported, not a recipient file

events.geography: United States; Virginia personal-auto insurance market
events.method: Structured extraction from the Virginia SCC public settlement summary
events.missingness: No policyholder identifiers, amount by consumer, receipt, premium re-rating, coverage continuity, residual loss, trust, or switching
events.exposure: State Farm reportedly issued policies or premiums inconsistent with filed rate information
events.alternatives_before_action: Consumers could contact the insurer, seek regulatory review, change insurers, or remain; individual choices are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Reported overcharge exposure and approximately $2.5 million aggregate restitution
events.choice_or_response: The insurers offered settlement and committed to accurate filings, filed-rate use, and monitoring; consumer response is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The insurers controlled rating/filing operations; SCC controlled investigation and settlement acceptance
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Restitution plus corrective controls for filed rates and ongoing monitoring
events.remedy_receipt: The SCC reports aggregate restitution paid; individual receipt, amount, and premium correction are not verified
events.durability_followup: Later premium accuracy, renewal, coverage, trust, switching, and recurrence remain open
events.immediate_outcome: A large restitution route and prospective rating controls are reported
events.protected_outcome: Some consumers may have recovered overcharges; individual protection is not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Residual overcharge, delayed payment, coverage disruption, and uncorrected account status cannot be identified
events.cost_risk_transfer: Settlement places correction and monitoring duties on the insurer while person-level recovery remains unobserved
events.later_outcome: No individual receipt, corrected premium, renewal, switching, trust, or exit is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: Regulatory attribution is visible; consumer fairness and trust judgments are not
events.public_or_collective_response: State enforcement is visible; consumer collective action is not
events.counterexample: A large reported recipient count does not establish that every consumer received adequate or timely correction
events.source_and_uncertainty: Virginia SCC public settlement summary; aggregate restitution and corrective-plan statements are regulator-reported, not a recipient file

events.geography: United States; Virginia health-insurance and behavioral-health network context
events.denominator: 1,680 consumers and 586 providers; approximately $346,000 reported restitution plus $118,000 to Virginia
events.method: Structured extraction from the Virginia SCC public settlement summary
events.missingness: No patient/provider identifiers, claim payment, network correction, care continuity, receipt, residual cost, trust, or switching
events.exposure: Contracting, credentialing, demographic, network-status, and fee-schedule problems reportedly caused inaccurate or delayed provider payments
events.alternatives_before_action: Patients and providers could seek correction, alternate providers, other payers, or regulatory review; individual routes are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Reported network/claims harm and aggregate restitution; care-level restoration is not established
events.choice_or_response: Anthem/Carelon offered settlement terms requiring claims, vendor, and data controls; consumer/provider response is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Insurer and affiliate operations controlled network/claims systems; SCC controlled inspection and settlement acceptance
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Reported restitution, treasury payment, and prospective claims, data, vendor, and testing controls
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate payments are reported; individual receipt, corrected claim, network restoration, and completed care are not verified
events.durability_followup: Future claim accuracy, provider participation, care continuity, patient cost, trust, switching, and exit remain open
events.immediate_outcome: A mixed consumer-provider restitution route and system-control response are reported
events.protected_outcome: Some affected parties may have received compensation and future claims may improve; health-access restoration is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Delayed payment, network confusion, delayed care, residual cost, and provider exit cannot be identified
events.cost_risk_transfer: Settlement shifts some correction cost to the insurer while care disruption and provider administrative burden remain unmeasured
events.later_outcome: No corrected claims, completed care, provider retention, patient recovery, trust, switching, or exit is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: Regulatory attribution is visible; patient/provider fairness and legitimacy judgments are not
events.public_or_collective_response: State oversight is visible; patient/provider organizing and political action are not
events.counterexample: Restitution and system controls can coexist with unknown care continuity and network outcomes
events.source_and_uncertainty: Virginia SCC public settlement summary; aggregate payment and corrective-plan statements are regulator-reported, not claim-level outcomes

arrows.from: insurance rating, notice, network, or claims-process error
arrows.evidence: The SCC summaries describe investigations followed by accepted settlements, aggregate restitution, and corrective-action plans
arrows.counterexample: The summaries do not provide complaint-level causal paths or identify every affected policy or claim
arrows.remaining_gap: Policy or claim identifiers, notice, correction request, and individual route history

arrows.evidence: The SCC reports restitution paid to defined consumer/provider counts and prospective monitoring or claims/rating controls
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate payment does not establish individual issuance, receipt, amount, or adequacy
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient payment, timing, returned payment, premium/claim correction, and residual loss

arrows.to: restored household security, coverage, care, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The SCC page reports settlement completion and prospective controls but no later recipient, patient, provider, or household outcome
arrows.counterexample: Payment can coexist with residual premium, coverage, care, or network problems
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-recipient or same-policy follow-up on payment, correction, coverage/care continuity, residual cost, trust, and switching

arrows.to: institutional learning and prospective process control
arrows.evidence: Settlement plans require additional rating analysis, filed-rate compliance, claims accuracy, vendor/system testing, and monitoring
arrows.counterexample: A corrective-plan commitment is not an observed future error rate, enforcement action, or durable correction
arrows.remaining_gap: Post-plan audit, recurrence, complaints, claim accuracy, network participation, and affected-unit outcomes

boundary: This ledger formalizes three Virginia SCC insurance settlements with regulator-reported aggregate restitution and prospective correction. It does not claim individual receipt, adequate compensation, coverage or care restoration, durable error reduction, trust change, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact official-page fields and source URLs are retained; no policyholder, patient, provider, claim, or payment file is downloaded.
